  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-amber-flashing { --led-color: #f59e0b; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-amber-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-blue { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-blue-flashing { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-blue-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-green { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-green-flashing { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-green-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-red-flashing { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-red-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='hpe/flom-817749-b21@'] .state-activity { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='hpe/flom-817749-b21@'] .state-activity { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='hpe/flom-817749-b21@'] .state-link { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='hpe/psu-865408-b21@'] .state-ok { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='nvidia/mcx4121a-lp@'] .state-activity { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='nvidia/mcx4121a-lp@'] .state-activity { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nvidia/mcx4121a-lp@'] .state-beacon { --led-color: #f59e0b; }

    g[data-ref^='nvidia/mcx4121a-lp@'] .state-error { --led-color: #f59e0b; }
    g[data-ref^='nvidia/mcx4121a-lp@'] .state-error { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }

  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-amber-flashing { --led-color: #f59e0b; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-amber-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-blue { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-blue-flashing { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-blue-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-green { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-green-flashing { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-green-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-red-flashing { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-red-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='hpe/psu-865408-b21@'] .state-ok { --led-color: #22c55e; }
</style>

  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='common/button-led-sq@'] .state-amber { --led-color: #f59e0b; }
    g[data-ref^='common/button-led-sq@'] .state-blue { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    g[data-ref^='common/button-led-sq@'] .state-blue-flashing { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    g[data-ref^='common/button-led-sq@'] .state-blue-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='common/button-led-sq@'] .state-green { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='common/button-led-sq@'] .state-green-flashing { --led-color: #22c55e; }

    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-amber-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-blue { --led-color: #3b82f6; }

  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-amber-flashing { --led-color: #f59e0b; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-amber-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-blue { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-blue-flashing { --led-color: #3b82f6; }

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="434.6mm" height="614.9mm" viewBox="0 0 434.6 614.9" data-device="dl160-gen10" data-view="top" data-ru="1" data-weight-min-kg="10.97" data-weight-max-kg="15.74" data-power-input="100-240 VAC per Flex Slot supply (the 865434-B21 supply -48 VDC, the 865428-B21 HVAC/HVDC)" data-psu-redundancy="1+1 with the redundant power supply enablement kit 866442-B21" data-fans="three single-rotor hot-plug fans with one processor, six with two; one more with the redundant fan kit 866438-B21" data-operating-temp-c="10 to 35" data-operating-temp-extended-c="5 to 10 and 35 to 45, approved configurations only" data-storage-temp-c="-30 to 60" data-operating-humidity="8 to 90% non-condensing, 28 C maximum wet bulb" data-altitude-operating-m="3050" data-acoustic-lwad="4.5 B idle, 5.1 B operating" data-cpu="up to two Intel Xeon Scalable processors, first or second generation" data-memory="16 DDR4 DIMM slots, up to 1.0 TB with 64 GB DIMMs" data-storage-controller="HPE Smart Array S100i embedded (SATA only); Smart Array modular and PCIe controllers optional" data-network="embedded 2-port 1GbE" data-bmc="HPE iLO 5" data-eol="announced" data-eol-announcement="https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/docDisplay?docId=a00021860enw" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="434.6mm" height="614.9mm" viewBox="0 0 434.6 614.9" data-device="dl160-gen10" data-view="bottom" data-ru="1" data-weight-min-kg="10.97" data-weight-max-kg="15.74" data-power-input="100-240 VAC per Flex Slot supply (the 865434-B21 supply -48 VDC, the 865428-B21 HVAC/HVDC)" data-psu-redundancy="1+1 with the redundant power supply enablement kit 866442-B21" data-fans="three single-rotor hot-plug fans with one processor, six with two; one more with the redundant fan kit 866438-B21" data-operating-temp-c="10 to 35" data-operating-temp-extended-c="5 to 10 and 35 to 45, approved configurations only" data-storage-temp-c="-30 to 60" data-operating-humidity="8 to 90% non-condensing, 28 C maximum wet bulb" data-altitude-operating-m="3050" data-acoustic-lwad="4.5 B idle, 5.1 B operating" data-cpu="up to two Intel Xeon Scalable processors, first or second generation" data-memory="16 DDR4 DIMM slots, up to 1.0 TB with 64 GB DIMMs" data-storage-controller="HPE Smart Array S100i embedded (SATA only); Smart Array modular and PCIe controllers optional" data-network="embedded 2-port 1GbE" data-bmc="HPE iLO 5" data-eol="announced" data-eol-announcement="https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/docDisplay?docId=a00021860enw" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="614.9mm" height="42.9mm" viewBox="0 0 614.9 42.9" data-device="dl160-gen10" data-view="right" data-ru="1" data-weight-min-kg="10.97" data-weight-max-kg="15.74" data-power-input="100-240 VAC per Flex Slot supply (the 865434-B21 supply -48 VDC, the 865428-B21 HVAC/HVDC)" data-psu-redundancy="1+1 with the redundant power supply enablement kit 866442-B21" data-fans="three single-rotor hot-plug fans with one processor, six with two; one more with the redundant fan kit 866438-B21" data-operating-temp-c="10 to 35" data-operating-temp-extended-c="5 to 10 and 35 to 45, approved configurations only" data-storage-temp-c="-30 to 60" data-operating-humidity="8 to 90% non-condensing, 28 C maximum wet bulb" data-altitude-operating-m="3050" data-acoustic-lwad="4.5 B idle, 5.1 B operating" data-cpu="up to two Intel Xeon Scalable processors, first or second generation" data-memory="16 DDR4 DIMM slots, up to 1.0 TB with 64 GB DIMMs" data-storage-controller="HPE Smart Array S100i embedded (SATA only); Smart Array modular and PCIe controllers optional" data-network="embedded 2-port 1GbE" data-bmc="HPE iLO 5" data-eol="announced" data-eol-announcement="https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/docDisplay?docId=a00021860enw" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */

    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }

    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='common/button-led-sq@'] .state-amber { --led-color: #f59e0b; }
    g[data-ref^='common/button-led-sq@'] .state-blue { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    g[data-ref^='common/button-led-sq@'] .state-blue-flashing { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    g[data-ref^='common/button-led-sq@'] .state-blue-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='common/button-led-sq@'] .state-green { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='common/button-led-sq@'] .state-green-flashing { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='common/button-led-sq@'] .state-green-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-amber-flashing { --led-color: #f59e0b; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-amber-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-blue { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-blue-flashing { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-blue-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-green { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-green-flashing { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-green-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-red-flashing { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    g[data-ref^='common/led-sq@'] .state-red-flashing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='hpe/sff-sc-carrier@'] .state-active { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='hpe/sff-sc-carrier@'] .state-active { animation: portrayal-blink 0.25s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='hpe/sff-sc-carrier@'] .state-do-not-remove { --led-color: #f8fafc; }
    g[data-ref^='hpe/sff-sc-carrier@'] .state-fault { --led-color: #f59e0b; }
    g[data-ref^='hpe/sff-sc-carrier@'] .state-firmware { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    g[data-ref^='hpe/sff-sc-carrier@'] .state-firmware { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='hpe/sff-sc-carrier@'] .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    g[data-ref^='hpe/sff-sc-carrier@'] .state-online { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='hpe/sff-sc-carrier@'] .state-predictive-failure { --led-color: #f59e0b; }
    g[data-ref^='hpe/sff-sc-carrier@'] .state-predictive-failure { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    @keyframes portrayal-seq-hpe-sff-sc-carrier-predictive-failure-member {

    g[data-ref^='hpe/sff-sc-carrier@'] .state-predictive-failure-member { animation: portrayal-seq-hpe-sff-sc-carrier-predictive-failure-member 1s steps(1, end) infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='hpe/sff-sc-carrier@'] .state-rebuild { --led-color: #22c55e; }

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="434.6mm" height="614.9mm" viewBox="0 0 434.6 614.9" data-device="dl160-gen10" data-view="bottom" data-ru="1" data-weight-min-kg="10.97" data-weight-max-kg="15.74" data-power-input="100-240 VAC per Flex Slot supply (the 865434-B21 supply -48 VDC, the 865428-B21 HVAC/HVDC)" data-psu-redundancy="1+1 with the redundant power supply enablement kit 866442-B21" data-fans="three single-rotor hot-plug fans with one processor, six with two; one more with the redundant fan kit 866438-B21" data-operating-temp-c="10 to 35" data-operating-temp-extended-c="5 to 10 and 35 to 45, approved configurations only" data-storage-temp-c="-30 to 60" data-operating-humidity="8 to 90% non-condensing, 28 C maximum wet bulb" data-altitude-operating-m="3050" data-acoustic-lwad="4.5 B idle, 5.1 B operating" data-cpu="up to two Intel Xeon Scalable processors, first or second generation" data-memory="16 DDR4 DIMM slots, up to 1.0 TB with 64 GB DIMMs" data-storage-controller="HPE Smart Array S100i embedded (SATA only); Smart Array modular and PCIe controllers optional" data-network="embedded 2-port 1GbE" data-bmc="HPE iLO 5" data-eol="announced" data-eol-announcement="https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/docDisplay?docId=a00021860enw" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="614.9mm" height="42.9mm" viewBox="0 0 614.9 42.9" data-device="dl160-gen10" data-view="left" data-ru="1" data-weight-min-kg="10.97" data-weight-max-kg="15.74" data-power-input="100-240 VAC per Flex Slot supply (the 865434-B21 supply -48 VDC, the 865428-B21 HVAC/HVDC)" data-psu-redundancy="1+1 with the redundant power supply enablement kit 866442-B21" data-fans="three single-rotor hot-plug fans with one processor, six with two; one more with the redundant fan kit 866438-B21" data-operating-temp-c="10 to 35" data-operating-temp-extended-c="5 to 10 and 35 to 45, approved configurations only" data-storage-temp-c="-30 to 60" data-operating-humidity="8 to 90% non-condensing, 28 C maximum wet bulb" data-altitude-operating-m="3050" data-acoustic-lwad="4.5 B idle, 5.1 B operating" data-cpu="up to two Intel Xeon Scalable processors, first or second generation" data-memory="16 DDR4 DIMM slots, up to 1.0 TB with 64 GB DIMMs" data-storage-controller="HPE Smart Array S100i embedded (SATA only); Smart Array modular and PCIe controllers optional" data-network="embedded 2-port 1GbE" data-bmc="HPE iLO 5" data-eol="announced" data-eol-announcement="https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/docDisplay?docId=a00021860enw" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

  <style>

    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }

    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
